clue.text: Caught that woman pinching fine necklace

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the pronoun's letters close around the next piece

parts.note: that woman is HER
fine, as in all right, is OK

explanation.surface: Someone is arrested while she pockets an expensive necklace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like theft in the story, but it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A choker is a short necklace worn tight around the throat.

clue.text: Where a judge may consult dictionary?

definitions.meaning: a judge's private rooms, where cases may be discussed out of court
A well-known British dictionary, much loved by crossword setters

explanation.surface: A judge looks something up in a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges hear matters in their private rooms, known as chambers; Chambers is also the name of a famous British dictionary publisher.

clue.text: Colour of coach-horses seen every so often

indicators.note: seen every so often tells us to take only every other letter of the hyphenated phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A coach-and-horses is painted a particular shade, glimpsed now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment and the shade it gives.

clue.text: Darkness resulting from cuts in essentially indispensable energy

indicators.note: in puts the snipping word between the two single letters that follow
essentially points to the very centre, the middle letter, of indispensable

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
cuts, as with shears, means clips

explanation.surface: A blackout caused by cuts to a vital power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes E, the middle letter of 'indispensable'; that E and E for energy go round CLIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclipse is the darkening of the sun or moon when another body blocks its light.

clue.text: Figure golf outside broadcast has fifty working up front

indicators.note: up front means the other pieces go in front of the letter for golf, which therefore comes last

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
working, as in switched on, is ON
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golf TV broadcast boasts fifty staff on duty at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' places OB, L and ON ahead of G.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a geometric shape, a rectangle longer than it is wide.

clue.text: Animated film that gets roasted?

parts.note: animated, meaning lively, is brisk
ET is Spielberg's famous film

explanation.surface: A cartoon movie that critics pan mercilessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roasted' suggests harsh reviews of the film, but it means cooked in an oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast, commonly slow-roasted.

clue.text: Beaten pair upset about dubious penalty opposition ultimately missed

indicators.note: about means the reversed pair goes around the rest
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pair is a duo

indicators.note: dubious means questionable, so the letters are jumbled
missed means a letter is left out of penalty
ultimately points to the last letter of opposition

explanation.surface: A beaten team are upset about a questionable penalty that the opposing side failed to convert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' drops N, the end of 'opposition'; 'dubious' rearranges the remaining PEALTY into TPLAYE; 'upset' turns DUO to OUD, which goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outplayed is to be beaten by a stronger opponent.

clue.text: Raised section of uncovered rigid beam

indicators.note: Raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of an exposed stiff beam is lifted up in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Raised' means read upwards, so the hidden REDRIG reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A girder is a large iron or steel beam used in building.

clue.text: Liberal at home initially beset by stomach pain

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the pain word encloses the rest

parts.note: colic is severe abdominal pain

indicators.note: initially takes only the first letter of home

explanation.surface: A broad-minded person stuck at home with a bellyache.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic in its lower-case sense means broad or wide-ranging in tastes, hence liberal.

clue.text: Suspect hip doctor is one offering sole treatment?

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A questionable hip surgeon claims to offer sole treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' hints at the only treatment, but it is the sole of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiropodist treats feet, including the soles.

clue.text: Jail locally from which associate escapes

indicators.note: from which, paired with escapes, says one word leaves the other
escapes means the ally's letters get out of the longer word

parts.note: something done locally is done internally, within one place
an associate is an ally

explanation.surface: A local prison from which an accomplice breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from which ... escapes' removes ALLY from INTERNALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine or imprison, especially in wartime.

clue.text: Guy ousting leader is clever

indicators.note: ousting leader means the first letter is pushed out

parts.note: a guy is a rope or cable that steadies something such as a tent

explanation.surface: A smart man takes over by deposing the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it is a guy rope, a cable; 'ousting leader' removes its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means skilled or competent, close to clever.

clue.text: Drug for each receiving a tattoo, feeling queasy

indicators.note: receiving means the outer word takes the others inside it

parts.note: per means for each
to ink someone is slang for tattooing them, and a tattoo is ink
someone queasy feels ill

explanation.surface: Someone getting a tattoo feels sick and wants something for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is an analgesic, a medicine for relieving pain.

clue.text: Commendable way report is prepared defending hospital

indicators.note: defending means guarding by surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the next piece
prepared means made up or put together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A report written in a way that defends the hospital deserves praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges WAY REPORT IS, which goes round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something praiseworthy deserves approval, which is what commendable means.

clue.text: Press hack finds old railway engine

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a hack is a horse for ordinary riding

explanation.surface: A newspaper reporter digs up a story about a vintage locomotive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press hack' reads as a journalist, but each word is a separate synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse was an old nickname for a steam locomotive.

clue.text: Reportedly twist beer can for inspection

indicators.note: reportedly means the clue words describe how the answer is spoken

parts.note: to twist something round is to screw it; a tinny is a can of beer in Australian slang

explanation.surface: Twisting a beer can so it can be examined closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close, careful examination of something.

clue.text: Branch of medicine Oscar practised moving around house

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the next piece
moving means the letters are shifted about

explanation.surface: Oscar worked as a doctor while moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like moving house, but it rearranges the letters of 'practised' into RTPAEDICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthopaedics is the medical specialty dealing with bones and joints.

clue.text: Characteristic to conceal occasionally one's route

indicators.note: to conceal means the first word hides the selected letters inside it

parts.note: a characteristic is a trait

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A habit of now and then hiding one's tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes N and S from 'one's', ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage or the way by which something is conveyed, a route.

clue.text: Memory loss means I misplaced article

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong place, so the letters of means are rearranged

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone forgetful explains that they mislaid an item.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for a loss of memory.

clue.text: Cleric rabbi's hoping to welcome

indicators.note: to welcome means the clue words take in, and so hold inside them, the answer

explanation.surface: A rabbi hopes to receive a visiting churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to welcome' hides the answer across 'rabbi's hoping'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior member of the Christian clergy.

clue.text: Drunk person disheartened Scotsman and EU citizen

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk

indicators.note: disheartened means losing its heart, the middle letter

parts.note: a person is a human
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A drunk, downcast Scot and a European fellow citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes M, the middle of HUMAN, leaving HUAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuania is a member state of the European Union, so its nationals are EU citizens.

clue.text: Pro inspires university rowing crew

indicators.note: inspires, read as breathes in, means the first word takes the letter inside

parts.note: pro, as in in favour of, means for

explanation.surface: A professional coach motivates a college boat team.
explanation.definitionFit: A four is a rowing boat crewed by four oarsmen, and its crew.

clue.text: Weak-looking female bird

parts.note: a rail is a marsh bird

explanation.surface: A female bird looks feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail describes someone delicate or physically feeble in appearance.

clue.text: Avoids chores as mum is annoying

parts.note: mum means silent, and SH is the call for quiet
irks means is annoying

explanation.surface: A lazy child dodges housework because their mother is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother but means silent: SH.
explanation.definitionFit: To shirk is to dodge work or duty, so avoiding chores fits.

clue.text: Chap occupies excellent day going round island

indicators.note: occupies means the man's letters sit inside the others
going round means turned about, so those letters are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written as AI
SAT is Saturday, a day
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man spends a fine day touring an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written AI; 'going round' turns the pair of words backwards, giving TASIA, split open by the chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is an island state of Australia.

clue.text: Rather attractive

definitions.meaning: ... as an adverb means rather, as in ... good

explanation.surface: Quite good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty means fairly or somewhat as an adverb, and nice-looking as an adjective.

clue.text: Heard on TV Torquay hotelier is bust

indicators.note: heard on TV means the answer sounds like a name spoken on a television show

parts.note: Basil Fawlty runs a Torquay hotel in the TV sitcom Fawlty Towers

explanation.surface: A TV hotelier from Torquay is overheard going broke.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a classic British sitcom set in a hotel in Torquay, a Devon seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust in its informal sense means broken, so not working properly.
